value: MWCC GC 1.2.5, -O4,p. WHETHER A STRUCT'S ARRAY MEMBER IS READ THROUGH A NAMED POINTER LOCAL OR RE-DERIVED FROM THE STRUCT BASE AT EACH USE IS A SOURCE-LEVEL CHOICE, IT IS VISIBLE IN THE TARGET BYTES AS A DISPLACEMENT SIGNATURE, AND IT DECIDES BOTH THE LOAD ORDER OF THE SURROUNDING EXPRESSION AND WHETHER MWCC HOISTS ADDRESSES INTO CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS. THE SIGNATURE IS FREE TO READ AND NEEDS NO BUILD: in `fnasm <unit> <fn> --diff`, a row pair where the target loads `lfs fD,0(rP)` / `4(rP)` / `8(rP)` while ours loads `lfs fD,K(rB)` / `K+4(rB)` / `K+8(rB)` for a member at struct offset K says the target held a POINTER to that member and our source did not; the row pair reversed -- target `stfs fD,K(rB)` against ours `stfs fD,0(rP)` -- says the opposite, that our source over-abstracted and the target re-derives. Both directions occur IN THE SAME FUNCTION and must be read per member, not per function. MEASURED, four sites across three functions in game/enemy/critter this run, every one a keep. (1) CritterCollideItems, pre-loop: source read `c->pos[0] + delta[0]` while the TU already declared `f32 *cpos = c->pos` and used it in the sibling `else` branch; switching the three `center[i]` reads to `cpos[i]` closed ALL FOUR `lfs` order clusters at 0x18-0x34 at once -- `fndiff --ops` went from 4 clusters + 3 IMMEDIATE rows to `opcode streams identical`, fresh fuzzy 95.9932% -> 98.7027%, commit 0a577abd3. (2) The same function's hitnode branch read `*(f32 *)(node + offsetof(CritterHitNode, position))` three times and passed the same cast as a call argument; hoisting it to `f32 *npos` closed the last two IMMEDIATE rows (a transposed `lfs` pair at 0xf0/0xf8), real 68 -> 66, fuzzy 98.8176%, and moved the whole function to `CLASS: RECOLOR ... all 33 differing word(s) are register fields`, commit dc2c70e2f. (3) CritterCollideWorld read `c->pos[i]` at five sites where the target holds the pointer in r31 across the entire body (`addi r31,r28,92`, then `lfs f0,0(r31)`, `4(r31)`, `8(r31)` and `addi r5,r31,0` as a call argument); adding `f32 *cpos` and routing every use through it was the single largest step of that function's reconstruction. (4) THE REVERSE DIRECTION, same function: `*(f32 *)((u8 *)c + offsetof(Critter, floorContact))` written at nine sites made MWCC hoist THREE addresses into r31/r27/r26 and keep them live function-wide, where the target simply re-derives `stfs f0,1080(r28)` / `1084` / `1088`; converting the nine casts to the GC-verified project-header field `c->floorContact[0..2]` (include/game/critter.h line 190, `f32 floorContact[3]; /* 0x438 */`, resolved with `gdlmem.py struct Critter --offset 0x438`) deleted three surplus `addi` -- ours-only went `-4 addi` to `-1 addi` and the opcode-multiset token count 15t -> 12t in one edit. THE MECHANISM AND WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: a named pointer local creates ONE address web with one definition point, so MWCC materialises the address once and schedules the dependent loads after it; re-deriving from the base at each use creates N independent address computations that the CSE pass may or may not fold, and when it folds them it must PARK the folded address somewhere -- which is a callee-saved register when the uses straddle a call. That is why case (4) cost three callee-saved registers and why freeing them was the precondition for case (3): in CritterCollideWorld the two are ONE lever, and probing either alone reads as a partial regression (case (4) alone measured `CONFLICT-UNARBITRATED real 153 -> 178` with the count moving AWAY from parity, which `probe.py --arbitrate` correctly refused to arbitrate). AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 6 applies verbatim: these are two variables on the same instructions and they need a joint probe. DISPOSITION FOR A MATCHING LANE: before spending any register or schedule probe on a function whose diff shows same-opcode `lfs`/`stfs` rows differing only in base register and displacement, read the displacement signature above and fix the POINTER-vs-BASE choice first -- it is a structural, semantics-preserving source question, it is usually also a de-fakematch, and in this TU it was worth real 153 -> 52 on one function and two closed load-order sites on another. It is NOT a recolor question and no postprocessor rule reaches it.
